advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Use row["title"] (the review-time reconstruction) for the disposable ticket's title, fall back to the tracker or prose line only when it is empty, and fix the docstring
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:237: """The reviewed ticket's title from the harness checkout's own tracker (read-only); the
src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:238:     labels file records the plan's description but not its title."""
src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:254:     title = (lookup or _tracker_title)(str(row.get("ticket_id") or ""))
src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/corpus.py:314:         "title": title,
src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/labels.py:566:             out_row = dict(row)  (labels rows are the corpus rows, so `title` is preserved)
src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:247:     except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — an unreadable title falls back to the first heading
advisory.finding: row_title ignores the reconstructed `title` that every labels row already carries. It looks up the ticket's CURRENT title in the harness checkout's tracker instead. The docstring's claim that 'the labels file records the plan's description but not its title' is false. So the disposable ticket can get a title from a later rename. For rows mined from another store via --store, the lookup misses and the code quietly falls back to the first prose line. Either way the reviewed title/plan pair can differ from what was historically reviewed.
scenarios: A ticket renamed after its review gets reviewed under the new title next to the old plan text
A row from a non-default store is not in the harness checkout's tracker, so the title quietly becomes the first prose line
advisory.suggested_fix: In row_title, return `str(row.get("title") or "")` first when it is non-empty, and only then call the lookup/prose fallbacks. Correct the _tracker_title docstring.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reproduce no_file_impact_reason/scope and children_material in the disposable store (or exclude/flag rows the harness cannot reproduce) so engines review the historical material
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:279-291: create_ticket(type, title, description) + set_file_impact(...) only
src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/corpus.py:317-321: "file_impact_scope": scope, "no_file_impact_reason": reason, "children": child_ids, "children_material": children_material
Committed results show harness artifacts, e.g. agentic: "Calls itself a 'child' but has no parent: ... parent_id is null" and "the ticket has an empty deps list"
advisory.finding: review_row seeds the disposable ticket with only type, title, description and file_impact. It drops the review-time material the row also carries: `children_material` (a container's children), `no_file_impact_reason`/`file_impact_scope`, and the `children` ids. Containers are reviewed with no children, and a plan that historically declared a no-file-impact reason is reviewed without it. Both engines can then hit floor blocks or raise findings about missing children, parents or deps that the historical review never saw.
scenarios: An epic/container row is reviewed as a childless ticket
A row with no_file_impact_reason and empty file_impact trips the Layer-1 floor and gets tallied as 'floor' rather than compared

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Record the corpus as its file name (or a path relative to the corpus root) rather than an absolute local path, and regenerate the committed JSON
evidence: src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/engine_comparison_results.json:2:   "corpus": "/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.rebar/worktrees/engine-review/evals/plan-review-gate/replay/labels-b3784f...jsonl",
src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:349:         "corpus": str(labels_path),
advisory.finding: The committed results file records `corpus` as the operator's absolute local path (str(labels_path)). That leaks a home-directory and worktree path into the repo and is meaningless on any other machine. The module itself says the path must not be hard-coded.
scenarios: Any reader or tool consuming the committed artifact gets a path that only exists on one laptop
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `labels_path.name` (the content-hashed name is already unique) for the `corpus` field.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drive retry through the runner seam: a fake runner raising a WAIT_AND_RETRY-classified error asserts one sleep and two calls, and a RuntimeError (NEEDS_INVESTIGATION) asserts `slept == []`
evidence: tests/unit/test_engine_comparison.py:231: `monkeypatch.setattr(ec, "_review_once", fake_review)` replaces an internal helper of the unit under test (review_row), not an external boundary.

src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:302-304: `if result["outcome"] == "error" and result.get("class") in RETRYABLE: sleep(RETRY_DELAY_S); result = _review_once(...)`. This retry gate is newly added code.

tests/unit/test_engine_comparison.py:124-128: the `boom` row raises `RuntimeError("provider exploded")` (class NEEDS_INVESTIGATION per line 161), but `_run` defaults `sleep` to `lambda s: None` and the test never checks that sleep was not called. If every error were retried, the outcome would still be `error` and the test would stay green.
advisory.finding: The retry test monkeypatches the module-internal `_review_once`, so it is coupled to that helper. No test shows that a non-retryable error (class NEEDS_INVESTIGATION) skips the sleep and retry, or that a second retryable failure stops after exactly two attempts. Code that retried every error, or kept retrying, would pass the current suite.
scenarios: The RETRYABLE check is dropped or widened, so every RuntimeError costs a 60s sleep and a second billable call, and no test fails.
Renaming or inlining `_review_once` breaks the retry test even though behaviour is unchanged.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_errors_and_floor_rows_are_excluded_not_disagreements, pass `sleep=slept.append` and assert `slept == []`. Replace the `_review_once` monkeypatch with a `_Scripted` runner that raises an exception classified WAIT_AND_RETRY on the first agentic call only. Add a case where both attempts fail retryably and assert exactly one sleep and an `error` outcome.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a `main()` test without --dry-run: an all-floor corpus returns 1, a decided corpus returns 0, and `--resume --out O` with a clean O makes zero runner calls
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:395-396: `if args.resume and args.out and args.out.exists(): resume = json.loads(args.out.read_text())`
src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:415: `return 0 if results["valid"] else 1`
tests/unit/test_engine_comparison.py:208: the only `ec.main` call passes `--dry-run`, which returns at line 393 before the resume/run/exit-code logic.
test_resume_* tests call `ec.run(..., resume=first)` directly, so the `--resume` flag → file read wiring is never exercised.
advisory.finding: The live (non-dry-run) CLI path of `main` is never run. Nothing tests its exit code (`0 if valid else 1`) or that `--resume` reads the previous `--out` file. For example, `main(["--labels", L, "--out", O], make_runner=...)` over a labels file whose only row is `_FLOOR_PLAN` should return 1, and no test checks that.
scenarios: An all-floor or all-error run exits 0 because the validity check is inverted or dropped, and the operator treats a meaningless run as a result.
`--resume` stops loading the checkpoint, so an interrupted live run re-bills every row.
advisory.suggested_fix: Call `ec.main(["--labels", str(labels), "--out", str(out)], make_runner=lambda cfg: runner)` with a `_FLOOR_PLAN` row and assert the return is 1. Rerun with `--resume` on a clean prior out and assert `runner.calls == 0`. If needed, monkeypatch `_tracker_title` to avoid reading the real tracker.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a summarize() case with historical_pipeline_verdict "INDETERMINATE" and both engines PASS, and assert historical n excludes it
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:175-177: `elif item["historical_pipeline_verdict"] in DECIDED: total += 1; hits += outcome == item["historical_pipeline_verdict"]`
src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/engine_comparison_results.json includes an item with `"historical_pipeline_verdict": "INDETERMINATE"` (ticket 01f8-11eb-4772-4c80).
tests/unit/test_engine_comparison.py: every `_row(...)` call passes "PASS" or "BLOCK", and test_a_run_that_compares_nothing_is_invalid uses "PASS".
advisory.finding: Excluding non-decided historical verdicts from the historical-agreement denominator is new behaviour with no test. Every test row has a historical verdict of PASS or BLOCK, so a row whose `historical_pipeline_verdict` is "INDETERMINATE" and both engines PASS (which should leave `n` unchanged) is never exercised. The committed results depend on this exclusion (6/10 over 11 rows).
scenarios: The `in DECIDED` guard is removed, so INDETERMINATE history counts as a miss and silently deflates both engines' historical agreement.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a load_rows test with an unverified row and out-of-order timestamps, and assert the filtering and ordering
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:60-61: `rows = [r for r in rows if r.get("verified")]` / `return sorted(rows, key=lambda r: int(r.get("review_event_ts") or 0))`
tests/unit/test_engine_comparison.py:28: `_row` always sets `"verified": True`, and every test builds rows in ascending `n`.
advisory.finding: Two corpus rules in `load_rows` are untested: it keeps only verified rows, and it sorts them oldest review first. Every fixture row is `verified: True` and written in ascending timestamp order. A row with `"verified": false`, or rows written newest-first, would expose a regression, and no test uses either.
scenarios: Dropping the verified filter would let unverified labels into the scored corpus and change the digest and the results.
advisory.suggested_fix: Write a labels file with rows [ts=3], [ts=1], [ts=2, verified=False] and assert `[r["review_event_ts"] for r in ec.load_rows(p)] == [1, 3]`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert rooting by observable store contents (e.g. the seeded ticket/fixture file exists under cfg.repo_path during the review) rather than the tempdir name prefix
evidence: tests/unit/test_engine_comparison.py:136-137: `assert cfg.repo_path and Path(cfg.repo_path) != tmp_path` / `assert Path(cfg.repo_path).name.startswith("rebar-eval-")`
src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:69: `with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="rebar-eval-") as d:`
advisory.finding: The store-rooting test asserts the temp-directory prefix of a different module (`rebar-eval-` from eval_solver.case_store). Its other check, `!= tmp_path`, is close to vacuous because the system tempdir is never pytest's tmp_path. Renaming the prefix would break the test with no change in behaviour.
scenarios: Changing the case_store prefix fails this test with no behaviour change.
advisory.suggested_fix: Inside `_Scripted.run`, record whether `Path(req.config.repo_path, ".rebar")` exists (or whether a seeded file_impact file is present) and assert that, instead of the `rebar-eval-` prefix.

dropped.finding: _default_labels picks `sorted(glob('labels-*.jsonl'))[0]`. The files are named by content hash, so lexicographic order says nothing about which corpus is current. Once a second labels file exists, the default run quietly picks whichever hash sorts first, which may be a stale corpus.
scenarios: After re-running plan_replay labels, the operator's default run compares engines on the older corpus

dropped.finding: The new 'Comparing the engines' subsection says the harness reads `evals/plan-review-gate/replay/labels-*.jsonl`. That path is fixed and relative to the repo root. The harness actually takes the labels file from `replay_dir()`, which is `<corpus_root>/plan-review-gate/replay`, and corpus_root defaults to `.rebar/evals`. The parent section tells clients that replay output goes under `<corpus_root>/plan-review-gate/replay/`. A client project that keeps the default corpus root would be pointed to a directory the harness never reads. The `evals/` prefix is only right for rebar's own checkout, which overrides corpus_root.
scenarios: A client project with the default config looks for the labels under `evals/plan-review-gate/replay/`. The harness actually reads `.rebar/evals/plan-review-gate/replay/`, or fails with `no labels-*.jsonl under ...`.
dropped.suggested_fix: Change the parenthetical at docs/llm-framework.md:632 to `(<corpus_root>/plan-review-gate/replay/labels-*.jsonl, or --labels <path>)` so it matches `replay_dir()` and the corpus_root wording already used at lines 595-597 and 613.
